mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand and construction activity, which typically leads to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST increases by more than 1% in the prior month but S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in over 50% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate falls below 0.10%, it signals aggressive monetary easing that reduces borrowing costs and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS falls below 0.10% but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of the subsequent 5 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high unemployment (UNRATE > 6.5%) and low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.10%) indicates a monetary policy response to a weak labor market, which typically triggers a short-term equity rally over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary easing with weak labor market
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE > 6.5% and FEDFUNDS < 0.10%, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% annualized), the Federal Reserve is likely to tighten monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as bond yields rise and equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 2.5% annualized), S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong labor market growth (PAYEMS > 100,000 monthly additions) consistently correlates with rising consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS increases by more than 100,000 but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of the subsequent 5 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 102.0, it signals robust manufacturing activity and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 102.0 but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST > 1080) and industrial production (INDPRO > 101.5) indicates strong demand and supply coordination, which typically results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST > 1080 and INDPRO > 101.5, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized), the economy is in a late-cycle expansion phase, which often precedes a market correction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized), S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
